answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, with honest participation earning small recurring rebates and proven fraud forfeiting the lock. A registry ties each stake to one active identity, so creating a swarm does not multiply influence without multiplying capital. The pearl of the design is that the nadir of an attacker’s return comes when detection slashes the stake, while the ridge of their cost rises with every identity they fund.
